Cluster Health: YELLOW
active: 3
zero redundancy (active == N)

Changes write acceptance on one node. One-node fencing does not necessarily block an entire quorum; use fence-quorum for deliberate quorum intervention. Re-run with -y only after reviewing the node and quorum impact.

Acceptance not given / too few selected reachable members

The command previews quorum impact and requires acceptance (-y bypasses the prompt). Fencing can interrupt writes and trigger rolling/recovery; it does not repair data. Re-run the reviewed command with -y to commit.

etcd list:
Error: Usage: --after-key and --after-key-base64 are mutually exclusive
# A compacted --revision instead produces a Network error.

Omit the prefix to explore all keys; list / searches only keys beginning with /. The limit controls page size, not the total count. When more=true, use the returned next_key_base64 and the same snapshot_revision for the next page. The context meta_prefix is never prepended.
etcd get: get reads one exact key and returns key metadata plus an encoded value. auto keeps readable UTF-8 text and base64-encodes binary protobuf data; this command does not decode Woodpecker protobuf fields. Use --revision to read a retained historical snapshot and -o yaml for YAML.
etcd cat:
CAEQACAu
# Encoded value only; binary auto output also explains its encoding on stderr.

Error: Usage: value is not UTF-8; use --encoding base64, hex or raw
# Only cat supports --encoding raw.

cat writes the value without an envelope. auto/text/base64/hex output ends with a newline; --encoding raw preserves exact bytes and adds none. Redirect raw output to a file for byte-exact inspection. Neither cat nor get changes the key.
meta log list:
# records: [] means this listing has no matching records.
# An undecodable record instead returns a configuration error.
Lists top-level log records, including unloaded history. records is a snapshot, not a list of live node writers. Narrow with meta log show; use the record revision for a patch.
meta log show: wp meta log show my-channel --etcd 127.0.0.1:32379 --meta-prefix milvus-prod/woodpecker
Error: TargetNotFound: target not found: milvus-prod/woodpecker/logs/my-channel

Shows the exact log key, ModRevision, lease and decoded fields. int64 values are decimal strings. A missing target means the key is absent in this namespace, not a damaged replica. Log truncation fields are changed with log truncate, not generic patch.
meta segment list: wp meta segment list my-channel --etcd 127.0.0.1:32379 --meta-prefix milvus-prod/woodpecker

# records: [] means this listing has no matching records.
# An undecodable record instead returns a configuration error.
Lists persisted segments under this exact log, including unloaded history. The parent log must exist. State and lastEntryId are metadata claims; probe/inspect physical data separately.
meta segment show: wp meta segment show my-channel 7 --etcd 127.0.0.1:32379 --meta-prefix milvus-prod/woodpecker

Shows authoritative persisted metadata and its embedded quorum when present. Active lastEntryId=-1 is an unknown final boundary; Completed/Sealed lastEntryId=-1 means finalized empty. A key/segNo mismatch blocks patching. This read does not verify local or object-storage payloads.
meta quorum list:
# records: [] means this listing has no matching records.
# An undecodable record instead returns a configuration error.
Lists separately stored quorum records. Modern segments embed their quorum, so an empty list can be normal; inspect meta segment show to see that topology. This group cannot patch quorum records.
meta quorum show: Error: TargetNotFound: target not found: milvus-prod/woodpecker/quorums/1

Shows one separately stored quorum by numeric ID; it does not fan out or test node health. es is ensemble size, wq write quorum, aq acknowledgement quorum. Modern embedded quorum is read through meta segment show.
meta check:
{
  "issues": [],
  "log_name": "my-channel",
  "scope": "metadata only; use segment inspect/log scan for physical data",
  "segments_checked": 2,
  "snapshot_revision": 18000,
  "state": "ok"
}

Checks log policy/frontier fields, segment identity/state/timestamps, embedded quorum structure and frontier bounds at one snapshot. Exit 9 plus issues means inconsistent metadata. state=ok establishes metadata consistency only; it does not prove payload readability or application progress.
meta export: Error: Config: create new backup file: open ./metadata-snapshot.json: file exists

Creates a new mode-0600 namespace snapshot. The file contains readable metadata for known protobuf records plus byte-exact value_base64, revisions and leases. Unknown/corrupt values retain bytes and encoding/decode errors. It is a metadata backup, not a payload backup or automatic restore command; an existing file is never overwritten.
meta log patch: wp meta log patch my-channel --patch-file ./log-policy.json --etcd 127.0.0.1:32379 --meta-prefix milvus-prod/woodpecker

Error: Usage: --apply requires --offline, --expected-revision, --reason, and --backup
# A stale revision or live writer lock returns StateConflict; no correction is applied.

Create log-policy.json using the walkthrough above. Only max_segment_roll_time_seconds, max_segment_roll_size_bytes, compaction_buffer_size_bytes and max_compaction_file_count are patchable (nonnegative; zero allowed). They are reserved metadata fields, not live runtime configuration. Preview writes nothing. Apply uses the target before.revision plus offline acknowledgement, reason and a new durable backup; unknown fields and leases are preserved.
meta segment patch: wp meta segment patch my-channel 7 --patch-file ./segment-repair.json --etcd 127.0.0.1:32379 --meta-prefix milvus-prod/woodpecker

Error: StateConflict: lastEntryId is below the log truncation frontier
# Other examples: key/segNo mismatch; Active segment requires lastEntryId -1; Sealed segment requires sealedTime.

Create segment-repair.json using the walkthrough above and independent data evidence. Writable fields are size, createTime, completionTime, sealedTime, lastEntryId and state. Lifecycle constraints remain strict; key identity, quorum and log truncation fields are protected. An existing invalid embedded quorum is preserved and reported in warnings rather than blocking a scalar repair. meta check will still report that unresolved quorum. A state edit does not create compacted files or repair replica contents.
log truncate:
Error: StateConflict: truncation cannot move backward or restore deleted data
# Active/empty targets, identity mismatches, stale revisions and concurrent updates are also rejected.

Preview requires a non-empty Completed/Sealed target and entry within 0..lastEntryId. Apply requires --apply --expected-revision (the log before.revision), --reason and a new --backup; no offline flag is required. The log and target revisions are compared and an audit record is written atomically. The frontier segment stays retained; earlier finalized segments become eligible for auditor/retention/reader-protected cleanup. Unchanged frontier means applied=false, unchanged=true with no artifacts. Verify application checkpoints first: metadata backup cannot restore reclaimed data.
diagnose:
wp --context milvus-prod diagnose --scenario write --window 30s --max-writers 16 -o json > write-report.json
# Current disk admission; progress rules remain inconclusive:
wp --context milvus-prod diagnose node-0 --scenario write --mode snapshot -o json
# Optional replica check: select the Milvus WP-client metadata namespace explicitly.
wp --context milvus-prod diagnose --scenario write --log-name YOUR_LOG --segment 0 --etcd http://127.0.0.1:2379 --meta-prefix YOUR_WP_CLIENT_PREFIX -o json
# Native read scenario:
wp --context milvus-prod diagnose --scenario read --window 30s -o json > read-report.json
# Optional reader check with a suitable reporting window and explicit WP-client namespace:
wp --context milvus-prod diagnose --scenario read --read-mode catch-up --log-name YOUR_LOG --segment 0 --etcd http://127.0.0.1:2379 --meta-prefix YOUR_WP_CLIENT_PREFIX --window 65s --interval 5s --max-samples 14 --budget 90s -o json
# Existing focused append check:
wp --context milvus-prod diagnose node-0 --scenario stuck-write --window 30s -o json

# Abbreviated illustrative output; inspect actual observations and coverage_gaps.

PartialCollection (exit 6): required metrics/ops/writers were unavailable or writer details exceeded the bound; report retained.
Budget exhausted (exit 5) / cancellation (exit 7): partial evidence retained.

Source-build capability. Reuses the WP service context and node Admin mappings. The write scenario checks append, writer-local buffer/flush trends, actual disk watermarks and optional explicitly selected log/segment quorum. Missing metadata does not fall back to another namespace. All includes these checks; focused stuck-write/read contracts remain compatible. --window samples from now; snapshot cannot prove a sustained stall. Queue pressure does not prove a disk/fsync cause, and missing replica observations do not prove quorum loss. Maintenance/object-store attribution remains an explicit evidence gap. Exit 0 means completed evaluation, not healthy; --fail-on-findings opts into exit 8 for warning/critical findings. Same-log completions cannot prove an individual op finished; resets, registry limits and missing evidence remain explicit. No external Prometheus, trace or Loki client is included.

Source-build capability. Reuses the WP service context and node Admin mappings. The read scenario separates success/EOF and pending server activity from leased reader progress and configured quorum evidence. Reader checks require explicit log/segment and WP-client etcd/prefix; there is no fallback namespace. The source client profile reports about every 30 seconds, so short unchanged-position windows are inconclusive. Fresh renewed attempts plus available data and catch-up expectation are needed for a no-progress suspicion. A missing replica is not quorum loss or corruption; a metadata end is not payload verification. Server ops lack reader identity, and duplicate numeric log IDs do not establish a tenant join. Existing focused stuck-write/read contracts remain compatible. --window samples now, not history.
